content:
Facts: An heir challenged a holographic will containing offensive statements against his spouse, alleging that the testamentary dispositions were dictated by an unlawful motive aimed at denigrating him and requesting a declaration of nullity.
Legal framework
Article 626 of the Italian Civil Code on unlawful motive in wills; Articles 1343 and 1345 ICC by analogy; general principle of irrelevance of motives; rules on testamentary interpretation.
Interpretative issue
Whether personal contempt or moral disapproval expressly stated in a will constitutes an unlawful motive capable of rendering the testamentary disposition null and void.
Principle applied
A testamentary disposition is null under Article 626 ICC only where the unlawful motive is expressly apparent from the will and constitutes the sole determining reason of the disposition, and only if such motive is contrary to mandatory rules, public order or public morality. Personal animosity, family resentment or contempt, even if explicitly expressed in the testamentary text, does not amount to an unlawful motive when it does not pursue a legally prohibited or antisocial purpose and does not replace the lawful cause of the testamentary allocation of the disposable portion.
